files.purpose: APIKeychain is the only Keychain gateway for the native API-key providers, and at B3 also the SecItem layer that MCPKeychain delegates to. It maps ProviderKind .deepseek, .meta, .zai and .commandcode to the fixed legacy accounts "DeepSeek API Key", "Meta API Key", "Z.ai API Key" and "Command Code API Key", and keeps one kSecClassGenericPassword item per account under the service AppInfo.name (overridable through a `service` parameter). Every value is trimmed and an empty one deletes the item. A write updates the existing item in place and adds a new one (kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked) only when none exists. A capture run reads nothing for a mapped provider.

feature_notes: B2 -> B3: the four per-provider wrapper enums (DeepSeekKeychain, MetaKeychain, ZaiKeychain, CommandCodeKeychain) are deleted upstream. Their account strings move into APIKeychain.account(for:) (:25-34), which carries the doc comment 'The accounts older builds stored keys under; changing one loses that key.' Callers now pass a ProviderKind: AppSettings.swift:444 uses key(for: provider, fallback: "") and :485 uses setKey(value, for: provider).
key(for:fallback:) now returns the fallback for a provider with no account before the capture-run guard (:11-12). setKey(_:for:) returns false for such a provider without writing (:21).

The write rule changed from delete-then-add to update-then-add (:50-57), which is the rule MCPKeychain already used at B2. SecItemUpdate succeeds -> true. Any status other than errSecItemNotFound -> false, and the existing item stays. Only errSecItemNotFound -> SecItemAdd with kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked. So a refused write no longer destroys the previously stored key. This matters for PR-PROVAPI-003, PR-PROVREG-088 and PR-PROVREG-239: under OD-0008 A6 a refused key is still not saved, but after relaunch the earlier key is read back instead of nothing.
set/read/delete are now internal-visibility statics with a `service` parameter defaulting to AppInfo.name. MCPKeychain.swift:12-22 delegates to them, and its own SecItem code is deleted in B3.
The header doc comment dropped the history note about each wrapper once carrying its own SecItem copy.

files.purpose: AntigravitySession drives Google's Antigravity CLI (`agy`) in headless stream-json mode, with one persistent process per thread. It launches with --input-format/--output-format stream-json, --print-timeout 30m, --add-dir <thread folder>, the normalized --model/--effort, --mode plan|accept-edits, --dangerously-skip-permissions for Full access and --conversation for a resume. It writes one {event:user} object per turn and maps init/step_update/result events to provider events, with tool rows, before/after file diffs, per-step context usage and cumulative-to-per-turn token spend. It also owns the static catalog (`agy models` collapsed by effort suffix, plus `agy -p /model` for the current model), sign-in status and plan limits (`/usage` and `/credits` headless envelopes with tab-separated text fallbacks). At B3 the edit before/after snapshots go through the shared EditSnapshots helper in SessionSupport.swift.

files.purpose: ClaudeSession drives Claude Code in headless stream-json mode (-p, --input-format/--output-format stream-json, --verbose, --include-partial-messages, --permission-prompt-tool stdio). It numbers its control requests (initialize, set_permission_mode, set_model, interrupt, stop_task) and routes the CLI's can_use_tool requests to app approvals, questions and plan approvals. Under Hydra it defines heads through --agents and --forward-subagent-text, keeps one stream state per head keyed by parent_tool_use_id, and brackets heads with task_started, task_progress and task_notification. It also maps stream events, assistant blocks and tool results to rows, turns the result's usage into context and spend, and gives a handshake-only helper for models and slash commands. At B3 its control replies wait through the shared PendingReplies, TodoWrite todos use ACPSession.parseTodoItems, and tool-result text uses ToolText.blocks.

feature_notes: control() now registers its reply with PendingReplies (:306-308). The id numbering ("droppy-code-<n>", pre-increment) and the envelope are unchanged. New with PendingReplies: a caller that is already cancelled throws CancellationError before the request is sent, and the counter has already advanced. A caller cancelled while waiting has its entry removed and resumes with CancellationError. A late reply for that id is dropped. The control_response case uses fail/resolve (:337-341) and didClose uses failAll (:684), with the same outcomes as before.

TodoWrite now emits ACPSession.parseTodoItems(input["todos"]) (:535) instead of the deleted content-only todos(from:). This adds the text/step/title fallbacks, drops blank items and accepts complete/done and inProgress/in-progress/active. PR-PROVCLI-063 is reclassified.

files.purpose: CodexSession drives `codex app-server` over line-framed JSON-RPC. It starts, resumes, forks, rolls back and compacts threads. It sends each turn with the mode's approvalPolicy, sandboxPolicy and approvalsReviewer plus a collaborationMode block, and maps item, delta, plan, diff, token-usage and turn notifications to provider events. It answers command, file-change, permission and user-input requests. For Hydra it tracks heads as child threads (thread/started, spawnAgent receivers, subAgentActivity notes), with per-head turns, spend trackers and models. Static helpers list models, slash-command skills and rate-limit windows, and spend a banked reset credit. At B3 the lead's own thread is never taken for a head, and the turn's model becomes the model its spend is attributed to.

files.purpose: CommandCodeAPI is the lightweight side of the Command Code CLI (`cmd`). It covers where the login lives (COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY, else ~/.commandcode/auth.json), `cmd status` sign-in parsing, and the account's rolling dollar windows and credits from api.commandcode.ai /alpha/billing/credits and /subscriptions, with plan-id naming. It parses the model catalog from `cmd --list-models`, honouring ~/.commandcode/config.json's chosen model and efforts, and holds the CLI's own reasoning-effort and context-window tables and the eleven-row seed catalog. It also embeds the TypeScript approval/MCP-bridge mod that headless runs load with --mod, installing it under Application Support/<AppInfo.name>/CommandCode. At B3 the tables and seed gain Claude Opus 5.5, and the seed also gains GPT-5.6 Luna.
